newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate dives at close on demand.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate dives at close on demand.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates ended down a hefty 200 basis points at 22.00 percent on Monday after heavy demand triggered by high rates reached in early trade, dealers said.
"Paper was very much on offer this morning so rates rose a little, but once rates were that high buyers stepped in and brought them down again," a trader said.
Overnight rates on Cetes had reached as high as 25.25 percent in early dealing.

Fixed-income analysts said they saw more volatility ahead due to market unease ahead of the July 1-2 Federal Open Market Committee meeting to review U.S. interest rates, and domestic mid-term elections on July 6.
Banco de Mexico injected 715 millon pesos during the session by assigned an overnight credit auction at a rate of 24.72 percent.
Bank paper paralleled moves by government rates and closed down 110 basis points at 24.25 percent.
A liquidity shortage of 715 million pesos was expected on Tuesday due to a central bank credit auction falling due.
